scenes.tts: Where in the cell does Hedgehog signalling happen? The first clue came from a screen. In 2003, Kathryn Anderson's laboratory studied mouse mutants from a chemical mutagenesis screen. Two had defects in the neural tube and limbs. Those defects pointed to broken Sonic hedgehog signalling.
scenes.visual: Title strip: Kathryn Anderson's lab, 2003. A screen chip makes two mutant cards; a red label 'defects in neural tube and limbs' joins them; an arrow leads to 'pointed to: broken Sonic hedgehog signalling'.
scenes.narration: Where in the cell does Hedgehog signalling happen? The first clue came from a screen. In 2003, Kathryn Anderson's laboratory studied mouse mutants from a chemical mutagenesis screen. Two had defects in the neural tube and limbs. Those defects pointed to broken Sonic hedgehog signalling.

scenes.tts: The damaged genes encoded intraflagellar transport proteins. That is the shuttle of motor proteins that builds the primary cilium, carrying parts up and down its shaft. Crosses placed their action after Patched and before the target genes. But a position in a sequence is not a place in the cell.
scenes.visual: Damaged genes chip becomes the intraflagellar transport chip; a cilium appears with a shuttle carrying a part up and down; then a short pathway Patched, gap, target genes where the chip lands; a dashed cell with a question mark appears: where in the cell?
scenes.narration: The damaged genes encoded intraflagellar transport proteins. That is the shuttle of motor proteins that builds the primary cilium, carrying parts up and down its shaft. Crosses placed their action after Patched and before the target genes. But a position in a sequence is not a place in the cell.

scenes.tts: The place came in 2005. Kevin Corbit, in Jeremy Reiter's laboratory, followed a tagged Smoothened. The tag let them watch where that protein went. When the pathway was switched on, the protein collected in the primary cilium.
scenes.visual: Cell with one cilium. Tagged Smoothened chips in the cell body; pathway ON lamp; the chips move up into the cilium.
scenes.narration: The place came in 2005. Kevin Corbit, in Jeremy Reiter's laboratory, followed a tagged Smoothened. The tag let them watch where that protein went. When the pathway was switched on, the protein collected in the primary cilium.

scenes.tts: Then the group changed the short stretch of Smoothened that sends it there. That protein stayed in the body of the cell. It could no longer pass the signal on. The protein lost its place and its job. So in vertebrates, the signal is read in the primary cilium.
scenes.visual: The address tab on a Smoothened chip is replaced by a red altered tab; the changed chips stay in the cell body, the cilium stays empty; the signal-passed-on arrow is crossed out; the cilium is ringed.
